gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate costs to leave idling 24/7 at the US average electricity rate. Measured idle draw × 8,760 h × $0.1816/kWh gives about $14/yr for the Aoostar WTR Pro 5825U, $21 for the Minisforum MS-01 i5, $24 for the TerraMaster F4-425 Pro and $39–48 for the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus. Added to today's maker-store price, three years of idle power comes to about $421 (WTR Pro), $532 (MS-01 barebone), $736 (DXP4800 Plus) and $772 (F4-425 Pro).
standout_why: I read bitdoze.com/best-mini-pc-proxmox (cited) and littlecompute.com/best-mini-pc-for-plex (cited). Bitdoze gives no measured idle watts for any pick and computes no electricity cost. Littlecompute lists idle power as 'TBC' for every unit and says 'no unit here has been metered yet.' The ChatGPT answers list 'low idle consumption' as a criterion but give no number for any box. Our own current page has no power or running-cost column. IdleWatt (cited once) lists about 13 W for the MS-01, but I did not open it, and per the search summary it gives no yearly cost and no NAS comparison.
decides: This supports the split ChatGPT keeps making, with a cost attached. If the drives go in the box, the Aoostar WTR Pro 5825U is cheapest to buy ($379) and to run (8.7 W average idle, about $14/yr). The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus costs about $315 more over three years, though it adds Quick Sync and the UGOS apps. If the media lives elsewhere, the MS-01 i5 at 13.2 W stays cheap to run, but only without an add-in NIC: a ConnectX-5 raised idle to 32.1 W, about $51/yr. Caveat: the reviewers tested with different drive setups. The DXP4800 Plus figure includes WD Red HDDs, the F4-425 Pro figure is SSD-only, and Notebookcheck didn't say which drives were in the WTR Pro. So the NAS gap partly reflects the drives, which the page has to say.
